answer: Edge-disjoint path quota. Each identity may route transactions only through a bounded number of distinct relay neighbors; sustained volume across many otherwise-unused links marks it as a hub. An onyx reputation weight accrues to identities whose traffic spreads across a wide inlet of independent edges rather than one dense cluster. At the zenith of the quota, further edges are refused until old ones decay. An attacker must provision and maintain many genuinely independent relay paths per identity, multiplying infrastructure cost far beyond cheap key generation.
